claim: Acceptance 41's RED-when — the plan's own designated feature-correctness core — cannot fire, because the fixture it names is refused by an unmutated part 3. Acceptance 43's RED-when has the identical defect.
evidence: 41 names the mutation 'compute the step count from the RAW DOM slot delta instead of DR47-11's reconciled list, against a fixture parent carrying a {false && <El/>} sibling'. DR47-7 part 3's own disagreement table rules that exact shape refused, and acceptance 42 row (b) gates precisely that refusal. The mutation touches only the step-count computation; part 3 still runs, so that parent never becomes eligible, no drag engages a drop index, and no POST is issued. Nothing lands one slot short — nothing lands at all. 43's RED-when inherits the same vacuity and names row (b), which acceptance 42 defines as refused.
impact: The two criteria that carry the blue line's promise through to the write would be believed green after a mutation run that could never have moved them — the shape AGENTS.md calls the most expensive kind of green there is, and the same class of false closure this plan already corrected twice.
required_correction: Restate 41's and 43's RED-when as a compound mutation that disables part 3 AND switches the step count to the raw slot delta, or name a fixture that passes all three predicate parts while the raw and reconciled indices still differ. If no such fixture exists, say so and state the compound mutation as the only available one. The criterion must name a mutation under which a write actually commits and lands at the wrong index, and must state what distinguishes it from acceptance 42's mutation so the two are not one gate counted twice.

claim: EG-2's and acceptance 21's backup RED-when — apply the fold's steps in reverse order — is a provable no-op over the fold this plan specifies, and the plan authorises a lane to drive only the backup.
evidence: DR47-6 C-ii ships one POST carrying steps: n with a single op and a single oid; the fold applies moveAdjacent n times with identical arguments, the only per-step difference being that expect is passed on step 1. A list of n identical operations reversed is the same list, so arm A's bytes are unchanged and the gate stays green under the mutation. EG-2 says 'Drive one, record which', so a lane that finds the primary mutation unavailable drives the backup, records a green, and promotes the probe to a permanent gate. The primary's availability is itself doubtful: moveAdjacent builds its own moduleContext(source) internally and exposes no context parameter, so hoisting the parse requires changing a shipped extractor signature — precisely the condition under which the plan routes to the backup.
impact: EG-2 is the gate on which DR47-6 — the owner's one-gesture-one-undo ruling and the whole no-new-write-class argument — stands or falls, and its stated fallback proof is unfalsifiable. A folded write whose bytes diverge from the sequential path would ship undetected, and the plan forbids the only escape by owner ruling.
required_correction: Replace the backup with a mutation that genuinely diverges the two arms — drop the step-1 expect check inside the fold, fold n-1 steps instead of n, or reuse step 1's resolved span offsets for step 2 — and state why it is refused-proof. If the primary parse-hoist mutation is retained, state whether it requires changing moveAdjacent's shipped signature and whether that change is in phase-47's scope, so a lane is not silently forced onto the backup.

claim: DR47-4's swallow latch has no ruled drain point and no acceptance leg for the gesture whose trailing click never reaches #dsh-stage — a case that exists only because DR47-2 rules out pointer capture.
evidence: DR47-4 rules the cell one-shot, consumed at the click exactly as takeTrailingClickSuppression is, and acceptance 12-15 cover commit, refusal, sub-threshold and double-consumption; none covers non-consumption. The shipped latch is drained unconditionally at press, ahead of ROW P and ROW D, but the plan never states that the reorder cell takes the same drain and never gates it. The gap is newly reachable: DR47-2 rules that no setPointerCapture is called at any point, and the plan derives that the click is dispatched on the nearest common inclusive ancestor of press and release. #dsh-panel is rendered outside #dsh-stage, so a drag released over the panel produces a click whose ancestor path excludes the stage and the stage's capture-phase click listener never runs. The two shipped drag machines never face this because their capture retargets the release onto the affordance.
impact: An engaged reorder released off-stage leaves the latch armed, and the user's next ordinary canvas click is silently swallowed — selection appears dead with no refusal string. This is the shield's recorded defect class re-entering through a door the no-capture ruling opens, and the plan explicitly contemplates the drag leaving the parent.
required_correction: Rule the drain point explicitly in DR47-4 as a press-time unconditional drain, stated as such rather than by analogy, and add an acceptance criterion under S47-2: a reorder gesture that engages and is released outside #dsh-stage leaves the next ordinary press-and-click selecting exactly as at HEAD, with a RED-when that removes the drain.

claim: The plan never states which element the reorder gesture takes as its subject, and DR47-5's refusal predicate is incoherent without that rule.
evidence: The plan rules where the press is armed, what stream carries it, which modifiers engage it, what the click does after, and which parents admit it — but nowhere states whether the moved oid is the PRESS TARGET or selectionRef.current[0]. Selection in this shield is resolved at the CLICK, not the press: dispatchForModifiers runs in the click arm, so at press time selectionRef still holds the PREVIOUS selection. A press on an unselected sibling therefore has two defensible subjects. DR47-5 compounds it by refusing on selectionRef.current.length > 1 alone, so pressing a third unrelated element while N=2 yields a Korean string naming a relationship that is not the broken one — the KI-17 shape the plan makes Principle 3. No acceptance criterion exercises a press on a non-selected element.
impact: Two readings produce different code and one of them writes move-up/move-down against an oid the user never dragged — a silent wrong structural write that every supplied gate passes. It also leaves DR47-5's Korean string firing on a case it does not describe.
required_correction: Rule the gesture's subject explicitly (press target resolved by the same rule handleShieldSelect uses, or the selection head), state what happens when the press target is not the current selection, re-scope DR47-5's predicate to that rule, and add an acceptance criterion with a RED-when for a plain drag on an element that is not in the current selection.

claim: 'Engaged' is defined two incompatible ways, and under acceptance 13 the plan silently changes what a shipped, ordinary, unmodified press does — contradicting its own Principle 1.
evidence: DR47-4 defines engagement as threshold-only, and DR47-5 confirms a refused gesture still engages past threshold. But S47-2's dependency line says the gesture asks the module whether to engage, which makes eligibility a precondition of engagement. Under the DR47-4 reading, acceptance 13 swallows the selecting click for ANY plain drag past threshold on ANY canvas element. At HEAD that click is not swallowed: the shipped travel condition is guarded by (shiftKey || selectionRef.current.length > 1), which is inert for a plain click at N <= 1. With the threshold at 4 px, a 5 px hand-shake while clicking an element in an ineligible parent — a population the plan's own scope-consequence says may be most of the corpus — would select nothing. The plan also never rules what threshold engages reorder.
impact: This is a behaviour change to the most common canvas interaction, it contradicts Principle 1 (the gesture may not change what any existing press does), and no acceptance criterion measures it — 11 covers sub-threshold only, 14 covers never-engaged. A lane can ship it fully green.
required_correction: Pick one definition of engaged and make DR47-4, DR47-5 and S47-2 agree; state the reorder engagement threshold explicitly and whether it is POINTER_DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX or a separate larger one; and add an acceptance criterion with a RED-when asserting that a plain past-threshold drag on an INELIGIBLE element still resolves selection exactly as at HEAD — or, if the swallow is genuinely intended there, rule that regression openly against Principle 1 and route it to the owner.

claim: The new steps wire field has no validation, no bound, and no failure behaviour, against a shipped precedent on the identical cost model that has all three.
evidence: DR47-6 adds one optional integer field to handleStructureEdit, whose current parsing returns 400s for every other malformed axis. The analogous fold the plan cites as its precedent bounds itself explicitly at MAX_MEMBERS = 32, whose own comment prices exactly this — the fold re-parses page.tsx once per surviving member inside the write lock at roughly 2.6 ms per parse, so 32 members hold the lock for about 83 ms — and returns a 400 batch-too-large. The reorder fold has the same cost shape (n parses inside commitWrite's lock; the plan concedes it is unmeasured), yet the plan rules no cap, no integer or positivity validation, and no 400. No acceptance criterion covers steps absent, 0, negative, non-integer, or absurdly large.
impact: An unvalidated repeat count on the write endpoint can hold the single write lock for an unbounded time, and a non-integer or negative value reaches the fold with undefined behaviour. It is also the one place the plan expands the wire contract, so leaving its refusal surface unspecified means no-new-write-class is asserted without the validation half being reviewed.
required_correction: Rule steps' validation and its bound in DR47-6 — accepted range, the 400 wording and family, and whether absent means 1 — state it as the fold's stop condition alongside acceptance 22's any-step abort, and add an acceptance criterion with a RED-when for each malformed shape.
